scams.name: Labuan Bajo Komodo Airport (LBJ) & Hotel Transfer Overcharge
scams.description: Komodo International Airport (LBJ) in Labuan Bajo is Indonesia's fastest-growing 2025 tourism gateway — flights up 40% year-over-year post-2023 infrastructure upgrade — and the arrival transfer ecosystem has scaled with the traffic. The legitimate taxi fare LBJ to Labuan Bajo town center (5 km) is Rp 75K–100K; to specific marine terminals (Boat Basin) Rp 125K–175K. The 2025 scams: (a) arrivals-kerb taxi kiosks quoting Rp 250K–500K for the 5-km transfer (real Rp 75K–100K); (b) 'hotel transfer included' bait where the 'driver' charges for a fabricated 'toll road fee' or 'harbour entry fee' at drop-off; (c) Grab/Gojek weak presence in Labuan Bajo (smaller city, thinner driver supply) — touts exploit this with 'Grab doesn't work here' claim (partially true but not a license to overcharge); (d) return-airport overcharge where drivers who bring you from hotel to marine terminal demand Rp 400K for the reverse trip at 5 AM pre-cruise departure. For older travelers: (1) most hotels in Labuan Bajo include free airport transfer with advance booking (email or WhatsApp 24 hours ahead) — use this; (2) if paying for transfer, book through your hotel at Rp 75K–150K (hotel-arranged) not airport-kerb taxi; (3) Grab IS available in Labuan Bajo but with thinner supply (wait 5–15 min) — typical fare LBJ-to-town Rp 50K–80K; (4) for pre-cruise early-morning marine-terminal transfers, arrange with your hotel the night before at Rp 100K–150K; (5) IGNORE every arrivals-kerb kiosk quoting Rp 250K+; (6) for late-arriving flights (most LBJ flights land 8 AM–6 PM; some 10 PM arrivals), airport taxi is the only option — negotiate Rp 150K firm before loading; (7) always ask for a printed rate card before agreeing to any transfer.
scams.avoidance: Use hotel's free airport transfer (most include with advance booking) If paying, book via hotel at Rp 75K–150K, not airport-kerb taxi Grab IS available in Labuan Bajo but slower — wait 5–15 min Pre-book pre-dawn marine-terminal transfer night before (Rp 100K–150K) Ask for printed rate card; negotiate Rp 150K firm before loading
scams.location: Komodo International Airport (LBJ) arrivals, Labuan Bajo harbour shuttle pickups, hotel-transfer pickups at airport exit, marine-terminal drop-off

scams.name: Komodo National Park Entry Fee Confusion ($500 Pass vs Real Rp 500K)
scams.description: Komodo National Park has gone through a turbulent 2023–2025 pricing policy change that scammers now exploit aggressively. In Aug 2022 the Indonesian government announced a USD250 per person 'premium pass' for Komodo Island — massive backlash caused the policy to be cancelled. The 2025 reality: the entry fee is Rp 500,000 (~US$30) per foreign visitor per day, paid at the park booth on arrival; Rinca Island (alternative dragon viewing, same species) has the same fee. The 2025 scams exploiting this confusion: (a) Labuan Bajo tour operators still quoting 'Komodo Premium Pass $250–$500 per person' as if it were legitimate — this policy was CANCELLED in 2022; (b) fake-ticket resellers online selling 'skip-the-line Komodo pass Rp 1.5M–2M' — there is no skip-the-line and real fee is Rp 500K at the gate; (c) in-park 'Ranger service fee Rp 500K' demanded at Loh Liang — rangers ARE required for dragon-proximity safety but the fee is included in the Rp 500K entry; (d) 'Komodo Conservation Foundation donation Rp 200K' demanded after entry — no such mandatory donation; (e) Pink Beach 'separate entry fee Rp 150K' — Pink Beach is INSIDE the National Park and covered by the Rp 500K day-pass. For older travelers: (1) the REAL 2025 fee is Rp 500,000 (~US$30) per foreign visitor per day — paid at the park gate on arrival; includes ranger accompaniment (mandatory for dragon proximity); (2) REFUSE any tour operator quoting 'Komodo Premium Pass $250+' — that policy is CANCELLED; (3) Pink Beach, Padar viewpoint, and Rinca are all covered by the same day-pass; (4) no 'skip-the-line' exists — the queue is 15–30 min even in peak season; (5) no 'mandatory donation' — refuse any post-entry donation demand; (6) Rinca Island has the same dragons as Komodo (same species) and is 30 min closer (less boat time) — consider Rinca for older travelers who don't need the 'Komodo Island' bucket-list checkbox; (7) confirm your boat tour includes the Rp 500K entry fee in writing — some operators quote boat price only and add entry at the gate; (8) bring Rp 500K per day per person in small bills (Rp 50K, 100K) — park gate does not take cards; (9) do NOT approach dragons without a ranger; fatalities occur annually.
scams.avoidance: Pay ONLY Rp 500,000 per person per day at the park gate — real 2025 fee REFUSE every 'Premium Pass' quote — that policy was cancelled 2022 Pink Beach, Padar, Rinca all covered by same day-pass Rinca Island has the same dragons — often better for older travelers Bring Rp 500K per person in small bills (park gate doesn't take cards)
scams.location: Komodo National Park entry at Loh Liang (Komodo Island), Loh Buaya (Rinca Island), Pink Beach, Padar viewpoint, Labuan Bajo park-entry booking offices

scams.name: Komodo Day-Tour Boat Operator Safety & Overcrowding Scam
scams.description: The 'Komodo day tour' from Labuan Bajo — typically covering Padar viewpoint, Pink Beach, Komodo or Rinca Island, and Manta Point snorkel — is the region's flagship excursion and hosts a 2025 safety-compromise ecosystem. The canonical 2025 pattern: tourists pay for 'premium speedboat 2-hour crossing' and get loaded onto a slow wooden boat with 6–8 hour crossings. The 2025 scams: (a) boat-type misrepresentation — 'fast speedboat 1-hour to Padar' becomes an old wooden phinisi at 3-hour speed; (b) overcrowding — 30+ passengers on boats with legal capacity 20; (c) missing safety equipment — no life jackets, no VHF radio, no first-aid, crew without proper training; (d) 'private tour Rp 8M per boat' when the same boat is sold simultaneously to 3 other groups; (e) no-show breakfast/lunch or food quality far below advertised 'fresh seafood' (rice + egg reality); (f) weather-cancellation scam — 'trip cancelled due to weather, Rp 200K refund fee' when actual weather was fine. For older travelers: (1) book ONLY through reputable licensed operators — Komodo National Park certified list, Klook, or Viator — NOT port-front touts; (2) specific 2025-reputable operators: Wanua Adventure, Komodo Tour Flores, Sunshine Bali Komodo, CN Travel Komodo; (3) CONFIRM boat type in writing (speedboat vs phinisi vs slow boat) + passenger count + food menu + safety equipment list; (4) for older travelers, SKIP the 3D2N phinisi liveaboard unless you're healthy — basic phinisi accommodations and rough overnight anchor sleep are not recommended for 65+; (5) one-day fast-speedboat tour (Rp 1.8M–2.5M per person with entry fees included) hits the highlights (Padar + Pink Beach + Komodo OR Rinca + Manta Point) with return same day — much safer; (6) verify life jackets for every passenger BEFORE departure; (7) VHF radio visible in cockpit; (8) review Google and Tripadvisor ratings for the SPECIFIC boat (not just operator) — accident history matters.
scams.avoidance: Book via Klook, Viator, or certified licensed operators only Reputable 2025: Wanua Adventure, Komodo Tour Flores, Sunshine Bali CONFIRM boat type, passenger count, food menu, safety gear in writing For older travelers, one-day speedboat tour is safer than overnight phinisi Verify life jackets and VHF radio BEFORE departure
scams.location: Labuan Bajo marine terminal (Boat Basin), Pede Beach harbour, Komodo day-boat operator kiosks, private marine-terminal drop-offs

scams.name: Komodo Liveaboard Overpromising & Quality-Mismatch Scam
scams.description: The 'Komodo liveaboard' (3D2N, 4D3N, 6D5N phinisi schooner cruise covering Komodo, Rinca, Padar, Pink Beach, Manta Point + overnight anchorages) is one of Southeast Asia's iconic experiences — and hosts a 2025 quality-mismatch scam ecosystem at every price tier. The 2025 scams: (a) price tier misrepresentation — 'deluxe cabin with private bathroom' photographed from a different boat; real cabin is a 4-person bunkroom with shared toilet; (b) itinerary cuts — promised 'Manta Point + Padar sunrise + Pink Beach + Kelor Island' becomes 2 of 4 sites due to 'weather'; (c) dive-operator bundling scam where liveaboard claims 'PADI-certified dives included' but operator is not licensed; (d) food-quality gap — 'fresh seafood daily' becomes rice + egg + instant noodles from day 2; (e) drinking-water scarcity (large-bottle water 'not included' with Rp 50K per bottle at sea); (f) dangerous boats without VHF, radar, life rafts, or safety certification. For older travelers — or anyone without strong boat experience — the practical defense: (1) book ONLY through established operators with 50+ Google or Tripadvisor 4.8+ reviews: Le Voyage, Calico Jack, Luxury Cruise Komodo, Samata, Sea Safari; verify via direct booking (not resale sites); (2) for older travelers (65+), choose mid-tier or luxury operators (Le Voyage 4D3N $1,500+, Samata $2,500+) — budget operators cut corners dangerously; (3) CONFIRM in writing: specific boat name (not operator brand), exact cabin type (photo from your actual cabin), exact itinerary, food menu, dive-operator certification, safety equipment list (VHF, radar, life rafts, AED); (4) avoid 3D2N overnight on-boat unless the cabin photos are verifiable; consider DAY-TRIP speedboat from Labuan Bajo (Rp 1.8M–2.5M) hitting the same sites with return to hotel nightly; (5) purchase travel insurance with marine/evacuation coverage (US$100–$150 extra for comprehensive); (6) verify the boat has radar and VHF — Flores Sea can be rough and remote; (7) if boat quality is grossly misrepresented upon boarding, you have legal standing to refuse and demand refund — don't board a clearly unsafe boat.
scams.avoidance: Book operators with 50+ Google/Tripadvisor 4.8+ reviews (Le Voyage, Samata) Older travelers: mid-tier/luxury tier ($1,500+); budget tier cuts corners CONFIRM boat name, cabin photos, itinerary, food, safety gear in writing Consider day-trip speedboat (Rp 1.8M–2.5M) instead of overnight Purchase marine/evacuation travel insurance; verify VHF + radar
scams.location: Labuan Bajo harbour liveaboard terminals, online liveaboard booking sites, marine-terminal boat-boarding, remote-anchorage overnight stops

scams.name: Pink Beach / Padar / Rinca 'Mandatory Ranger' & Photo-Spot Fee Padding
scams.description: Beyond the headline Komodo dragon experience, the secondary Komodo National Park sites (Pink Beach, Padar viewpoint, Rinca Island, Kelor, Kanawa) host a 2025 add-on fee scam layered on the core Rp 500K entry. The 2025 scams: (a) 'mandatory Pink Beach ranger Rp 300K' — no ranger is required at Pink Beach (it's a public beach inside the park, day-pass covers access); (b) Padar viewpoint 'summit fee Rp 150K' — the 1-hour uphill hike has no separate fee, day-pass covers it; (c) 'best photo spot access Rp 100K' at Padar's Instagram-famous viewpoint — no such fee exists; (d) Rinca Island 'separate entry Rp 250K' — Rinca is in the same park, same Rp 500K day-pass; (e) Kelor Island 'snorkel gear hire Rp 150K' when your boat-tour operator should include it; (f) 'conservation fundraiser' requested by park rangers post-photo for 'dragon medication'. For older travelers: (1) the ONE Rp 500,000 day-pass covers Komodo Island, Rinca Island, Padar Island, Pink Beach, Kelor, Kanawa, and Manta Point — NO additional per-site fees exist for foreign tourists; (2) REFUSE every 'Pink Beach ranger', 'Padar summit', 'best photo spot' fee claim — none is legitimate; (3) Padar summit requires 1-hour uphill hike (sometimes wet stairs in rainy season) — for older travelers with knee issues, view from the mid-rim or skip; (4) Komodo/Rinca dragons — rangers ARE mandatory for proximity safety (included in entry); walk in a single line behind ranger, keep 5m distance from dragons, no flash photography; (5) Kelor Island snorkel gear — if your boat didn't include it, ask about operator refund; don't pay Rp 150K onsite for low-quality rental; (6) refuse any post-photo 'conservation fundraiser' request — donate directly to Komodo Survival Program online if wanting to help; (7) carry Rp 500K for entry in small bills (50K, 100K); (8) respect wildlife — dragons have attacked tourists getting too close; photograph with zoom lens from distance.
scams.avoidance: ONE Rp 500,000 day-pass covers ALL park sites — Komodo/Rinca/Padar/Pink Beach REFUSE every 'ranger fee', 'summit fee', 'photo-spot fee' claim Rangers for dragon-proximity ARE included in entry — don't pay extra Carry Rp 500K per person in small bills (50K, 100K) for park gate Donate to Komodo Survival Program online if wanting to support conservation
scams.location: Pink Beach (Komodo National Park), Padar Island viewpoint summit, Rinca Island (Loh Buaya entry), Kelor Island snorkel stop, Kanawa Island approach

scams.name: Labuan Bajo ATM Skimming & Remote-Area Cash-Fraud
scams.description: Labuan Bajo's rapid 2020–2025 tourism growth has outpaced its banking infrastructure — and freestanding ATMs in tourist-heavy areas have become a 2025 skimming target. The remote-area context amplifies the risk: cards cloned in Labuan Bajo are often used within 1–2 hours at Bali or Jakarta merchants before bank fraud detection kicks in. The 2025 patterns: (a) freestanding ATMs on Labuan Bajo main street (near Boat Basin) with card-reader overlays and pinhole cameras — same skimmer crews rotating through Bali, Lombok, Labuan Bajo; (b) hotel-lobby ATM installations by independent operators (not bank-branded) that are high-risk; (c) marine-terminal 'cash-only' merchant zones where tour operators demand cash then provide no receipt (chargeback-proof); (d) 'ATM not working, try this other one' direction to a specific skimmer-compromised machine; (e) hotel cash-exchange at 5–10% below Bank Indonesia rate; (f) Komodo-area rural merchants with tampered calculators showing wrong conversion. For older travelers: (1) withdraw a 3–5 day cash budget BEFORE flying to Labuan Bajo — bring Rp 4M–8M (US$250–$500) from a Bali bank-branch ATM; (2) if you must withdraw in Labuan Bajo, use ONLY ATMs INSIDE Bank BNI, BRI, or Mandiri branches on Jl. Soekarno-Hatta (main street) during business hours (8 AM–4 PM Mon–Fri); (3) cover keypad when entering PIN; wiggle card slot before inserting; (4) AVOID every freestanding, hotel-lobby, or marine-terminal ATM; (5) set low daily withdrawal limits (Rp 1.5M–2M) and real-time transaction alerts on your bank app; (6) for cash exchange, use reputable licensed money changers — AVOID hotel-reception exchange (5–10% padded); (7) dedicated travel debit card separate from main account; (8) if skimmed, contact your bank IMMEDIATELY (even from Labuan Bajo, hotel Wi-Fi + WhatsApp) and file police report at Polres Manggarai Barat; chargeback documentation is critical; (9) credit-card surcharges at Labuan Bajo merchants should be 0–3% max — refuse any 5%+ surcharge.
scams.avoidance: Withdraw 3–5 day cash budget in BALI before flying — Rp 4M–8M buffer If withdrawing in Labuan Bajo, use ONLY BNI/BRI/Mandiri BRANCHES during business hours AVOID all freestanding, hotel, or marine-terminal ATMs Set low daily withdrawal limits and real-time transaction alerts For exchange, use licensed money changers; avoid hotel-reception rate-padding
scams.location: Labuan Bajo main street ATMs, marine-terminal cash kiosks, hotel lobby ATMs, Komodo-area cash-only merchant zones
